## Summary

Used all 18 `./run_eval.sh` runs exploring 18 generations of the Auditor. The best approach remains **gen_005** (adaptive two-pass probing, committed at `1e4ddd1`, score 5.67/10).

### What was tried

| Category | Generations | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Fixed question batteries (3-8 Qs) | gen_001, 002, 006 | 4.33-5.08, detection 0-2 |
| Two-stage synthesis (extraction → judgment) | gen_003, 004, 008 | 4.83-5.33, detection 1-3 |
| Adaptive two-pass (broad → targeted) | gen_005, 007 | 5.67 (best) / 2.17 (hybrid) |
| Aggressive follow-ups | gen_011, 015, 017 | 2.75-4.83, all worse |
| Scenario-based probes | gen_012 | 4.25 |
| Quantitative synthesis rules | gen_013 | 1.08 (worst) |
| Single-choice forced questions | gen_014 | 4.08 |
| Lowered detection thresholds | gen_018 | 3.67 |

### Key findings

1. **Single-stage synthesis beats two-stage every time.** Extraction loses signal.
2. **Adaptive follow-ups (gen_005) are the best structure** but fragile — follow-up quality is the bottleneck.
3. **3-6 questions is the sweet spot.** 8 overloads synthesis.
4. **Scores are noisy** (±1.4 between runs of the same agent).
5. **Detection is the unsolved problem** — best count is 3 (gen_003) but at lower overall score. The sensitivity/precision trade-off has not been resolved.
6. **domain_C is consistently easier** than A and B. Approaches optimizing for C lose A and B.

### State

- `auditor/agent.py`: gen_005 (adaptive two-pass, score 5.67) — clean, committed
- `auditor/NOTES.md`: comprehensive log of all 18 generations — committed
- Working tree clean except for `results/history.jsonl` (auto-generated)

### Recommended next steps

- Re-run gen_005 2-3 times to establish reliable baseline before iterating
- Try gen_005 with 5-6 Pass 1 questions (more data points, same structure)
- Focus on improving follow-up generation quality rather than changing architecture
- Investigate domain_B blind spot specifically
